summary: Checked the change to custom deployment env var names. All server secrets are read through lib/env.ts. getOpenAiApiKey checks openai_api_key, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then openai_apikey. getGeminiApiKey checks geminiapi_script, then GEMINI_API_KEY. getGoogleAppsScriptUrl checks google_gorm_api, then GOOGLE_APPS_SCRIPT_URL, then GOOGLE_FORM_API. Values are trimmed, so blank or whitespace values fall through to the next name. No old uppercase names are read anywhere in app/, lib/, components/, hooks/, proxy.ts or next.config.js outside lib/env.ts. Supabase NEXT_PUBLIC names are unchanged. npm test passed 28/28 (including the new custom env names test), npx tsc --noEmit exited 0, and npm run lint reported 0 errors and 4 warnings. npm run build succeeded with exit 0 and 17 routes; it was run in an isolated copy of the repo with GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_APPS_SCRIPT_URL unset, so the .next folder of the running :3005 server was not touched. The custom names stay as runtime process.env reads in the server chunks (not inlined) and do not appear in .next/static. The :3005 server was confirmed to be running with geminiapi_script and google_gorm_api set (values not read). On it, test_unauth_api.py passed 17/17: every protected endpoint returns JSON 401, export with invalid params returns 400, and the public pages render. Live tsx check with only geminiapi_script set: provider is 'gemini', createEmbedding returns a 1536-dim vector with norm 1.0. With no AI keys, importing lib/ai does not throw, and calling getAiProvider throws a clear message that the routes catch.
action_items: Optional: update the stale note in /app/memory/PRD.md that says 'set GEMINI_API_KEY in Vercel'; it should now say geminiapi_script.

critical_code_review_comments: lib/env.ts is small, correct and side-effect free: nothing is read at import time.
GEMINI_MODEL, OPENAI_MODEL and UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY are still read directly. That is fine because they are optional and have defaults or are guarded.
In next.config.js, the env block maps supabase_publicurl and supabase_anonkey to the NEXT_PUBLIC names as build-time fallbacks. This is fine: these are public values.
